qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Exclusive regulated service territories across 8 Western and Midwestern states (Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, etc.) with non-replicable transmission and distribution assets. Rate-base cost-of-service model provides authorized ROE (~9.3-10.0%) and fuel-clause riders passing generation and operating expenses to captive rate-payers. Primary erosion threats stem from extreme-weather wildfire liabilities in Colorado and Texas, rising ratepayer resistance to clean-energy capital expenditure rate hikes, and regulatory lag.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Balance Sheet & Cash Conversion). Regulated electric and gas monopoly across 8 states with an unreplicable transmission network, but disqualified by structural utility economics: 10-year median ROIC of 4.8%, deeply negative free cash flow after capex ($10.9B capex vs $4.1B OCF in FY2025), heavy debt load of $31.8B (15.8x net income), and thin interest coverage of 1.76x requiring perpetual debt issuance.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 4.8% (2016-2025 range 4.0%-6.6%). TTM operating cash flow of $4,083M is overwhelmed by $10,908M in capital expenditures, producing -$6.8B in annual free cash drain. Long-term debt has grown from $14.2B in 2016 to $31.8B in 2025. With TTM EBIT of $2,583M and interest expense of $1,468M, interest coverage is just 1.76x. Despite resolving the 2021 Marshall Fire ($640M settlement) and stabilizing S&P/Fitch credit ratings at BBB+ (outlook Stable), continuous external debt and hybrid issuance is mandatory to support the $45B+ capital plan.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
